summary: Samsung Electronics' leading-edge logic foundry project in Taylor, Texas, announced in November 2021 as an estimated USD 17 billion fab near its Austin plant. The 2024 CHIPS award describes two logic fabs and an R&D fab in Taylor plus an Austin expansion. Construction began in 2022. The original second-half 2024 start slipped; Tesla signed a supply contract tied to the fab in 2025; and in October 2026 Samsung placed the start of operations at its first Taylor fab in its 2027 outlook. A second fab is planned, with construction from late 2026 and production targeted for 2030.

location.note: In Williamson County, roughly 25 km northeast of Samsung's existing Austin site, with which it shares infrastructure.

notes: The April 2024 preliminary terms also included an advanced packaging plant in Taylor for 3D HBM and 2.5D packaging. The December 2024 final award release and the NIST project page list only the two logic fabs, the R&D fab and the Austin expansion, so packaging is not recorded as a segment here. In February 2026 Taylor city officials had issued temporary certificates of occupancy for about 88,000 sq ft of Fab 1, and the same report said EUV tool testing was expected to start the following month. The Austin FD-SOI expansion covered by the same award is not part of this record.

registry_records.note: The registry row is filed under Austin; the award covers the new Taylor fabs and the Austin expansion.

review.changes: Set the operator to Samsung Austin Semiconductor, the subsidiary that Samsung's Taylor page says will run the site and that NIST names as award recipient, with Samsung Electronics as owner; marked the 2021 site size as planned and added the reported 1,268-acre campus size; replaced the Belgian newsroom copy of the third-quarter 2026 results with the global release.
